notes.summary: Probability = favourable outcomes / total outcomes. Rare in Tier 1, about one question in Tier 2. Coins, dice, cards and balls cover almost everything.

concepts.title: Basics
concepts.body: P(E) = favourable / total, always between 0 and 1. P(not E) = 1 − P(E). P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).

concepts.title: Sample spaces
concepts.body: One coin: 2; two coins: 4; three coins: 8. One die: 6; two dice: 36. A deck has 52 cards: 4 suits × 13, 4 kings, 12 face cards, 26 red.

concepts.title: Drawing without replacement
concepts.body: Use combinations: number of ways to choose r from n = <sup>n</sup>C<sub>r</sub> = n! / (r!(n − r)!).

varieties.name: Coins and dice
varieties.how: List or count outcomes from the sample space (2<sup>n</sup> for coins, 36 for two dice).

example.q: Probability of getting a sum of 7 with two dice?

varieties.name: Cards
varieties.how: Count favourable cards; for “or”, subtract the overlap.

example.q: Probability of drawing a red card?

varieties.name: Balls from a bag
varieties.how: Use combinations for drawing more than one ball.

example.q: Bag: 3 red, 2 green. One ball drawn. P(green)?

tips: Doubles in two dice: 6 out of 36.
traps: In “king or heart”, the king of hearts is counted twice; subtract it once.

formulas.name: Addition rule
formulas.expr: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

questions.q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
Two coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.solution:
Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT.
P(no head) = 1/4.
P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 8?
A card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king or a heart?
questions.solution:
Kings = 4, hearts = 13, king of hearts counted twice.
Favourable = 4 + 13 − 1 = 16.
P = 16/52 = 4/13.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that both are red?
A bag contains 4 white and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that one is white and the other is black?
